topic: Governance must live in the data layer
angle: If agents can act, your brakes must be data-level, not UI-level.
sourceTitle: When agents act on their own, governance has to live in the data layer
linkedinPost:
Most AI governance I see is a UI pop-up asking for approval. That’s theater.

VentureBeat makes the key point: as you give agents autonomy, your real brakes must live in the data layer—where actions actually happen.

In production, the risky moment isn’t a pretty confirmation screen; it’s the write to a system of record. If an agent tries to do something it shouldn’t, the data plane should block it by policy, every time.

Patterns that work: policy-as-data (central policy engine), attribute-based access (down to row/field), pre-commit checks with dry-run mode, and immutable decision logs. Put guardrails at integration points, not only in the app layer.

Metrics that matter: unauthorized actions blocked, false blocks (with fast appeal), and mean time to policy change. If you can’t show an end-to-end audit of “who/what/why” for an agent action, you don’t have governance—you have hopes.

Where do your brakes live today: UI, app, or data? #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
